# Reference Adapter

Every page in this section extends one adapter, `ChatAdapter`, that connects
Kedi to a chat backend with tool calling and JSON Schema output. The code on
these pages is complete: the documentation test suite assembles the
`python title="..."` blocks into modules and runs them through real Kedi
programs.

The adapter is about 170 lines. It implements:

| Protocol or attribute | Defined in | Section |
|---|---|---|
| `kind`, `shortname`, `capabilities` | `kedi.agent_adapter.AgentAdapter` | [Overview](index.md) |
| `invoke`, `invoke_sync`, `produce`, `produce_sync` | `kedi.agent_adapter.AgentAdapter` | [Calls](#calls) |
| `default_model`, `profile_override` | `kedi.agent_adapter.meta.SupportsProfileOverride` | [Profiles](#profiles) |
| `tool_scope`, `register_tool` | `kedi.agent_adapter.SupportsToolRegistration` | [Tools](#tools) |

Later pages add subagents, conversations, and the other optional protocols to
the same class.

## The Backend

The backend stands in for your provider SDK. It receives one rendered request
and returns one reply: text, a decoded JSON value, or tool calls.

```python title="backend.py"
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolCall:
    id: str
    name: str
    arguments: dict[str, Any]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reply:
    text: str | None = None
    data: Any = None
    tool_calls: tuple[ToolCall, ...] = ()
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BackendRequest:
    model: str
    instructions: str | None
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
    tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    temperature: float | None = None


class Backend(Protocol):
    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply: ...
```

A real backend translates `BackendRequest` into its provider call: `instructions`
becomes the system or developer message, `messages` the conversation, `tools` the
provider's tool declarations, and `output_schema` its structured-output or
response-format option.

## The Adapter

```python title="chat_adapter.py"
from __future__ import annotations

import inspect
import json
from collections.abc import Generator, Sequence
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from typing import Any

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic_core import to_jsonable_python

from kedi.agent_adapter import AdapterCapabilities, AgentAdapterKind, HookDeniedError, ToolSpec
from kedi.agent_adapter.approvals.policy import ToolApprovalDenied
from kedi.agent_adapter.execution import run_sync
from kedi.agent_adapter.invocation import InvocationUsage, report_invocation
from kedi.agent_adapter.output_schema import build_output_model
from kedi.agent_adapter.request_retry import request_retry_limit, wait_for_request_retry
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.errors import correctable_tool_error
from kedi.agent_adapter.tools.execution import validate_tool_arguments
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile, AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
from kedi.agent_profile.settings import KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS
from kedi.run_budget import admit_run_operation

from backend import Backend, BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall


class ChatAdapter:
    kind: AgentAdapterKind = "agent-framework"
    shortname = "chat"
    capabilities = AdapterCapabilities(
        supports_structured_output=True,
        supports_tool_registration=True,
        supports_artifacts=True,
        supports_profile_override=True,
        supports_model_override=True,
        supports_effort=False,
        supports_settings=True,
        settings=frozenset({"temperature"}),
        supports_mcp=False,
        supports_request_budget=True,
        supports_tool_attempt_budget=True,
    )

    def __init__(
        self, backend: Backend, *, model: str, max_steps: int = 8, request_retries: int = 2
    ) -> None:
        self._backend = backend
        self._model = model
        self._max_steps = max_steps
        self._request_retries = request_retries
        self._profiles: ContextVar[tuple[AgentProfile, ...]] = ContextVar(
            f"chat_profiles_{id(self)}", default=()
        )
        self._tools: ContextVar[tuple[ToolSpec, ...]] = ContextVar(
            f"chat_tools_{id(self)}", default=()
        )
```

The `ContextVar`s give every concurrent call, thread, and subagent its own
profile stack and tool set. Kedi runs template blocks in parallel and children
in background tasks, so state stored on `self` would leak between them.

### Profiles

```python title="chat_adapter.py"
    def default_model(self) -> str | None:
        return self._model

    @property
    def active_profile(self) -> AgentProfile:
        stack = self._profiles.get()
        return stack[-1] if stack else AgentProfile.empty()

    @contextmanager
    def profile_override(self, profile: AgentProfile) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
        unsupported = [
            name
            for name, present in (
                ("effort", profile.effort is not None),
                ("mcp", bool(profile.mcp_servers)),
            )
            if present
        ]
        unsupported += sorted(
            set(profile.settings) - KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS - self.capabilities.settings
        )
        if unsupported:
            raise AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported(
                f"{self.shortname} does not support profile fields: {', '.join(unsupported)}"
            )
        token = self._profiles.set((*self._profiles.get(), profile))
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._profiles.reset(token)
```

Kedi enters `profile_override(profile)` around every call. Once an adapter
implements it, Kedi no longer rejects profile fields on the adapter's behalf,
so the adapter must refuse what it cannot honor. Settings named in
`KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS` (`context_limit`, `media_limit`, `request_retries`,
`tool_reason`, `voice`) belong to Kedi and are never an error; see [Profiles, Models,
and Settings](profiles.md). The profile's `> instructions:`
need no handling here: Kedi already renders them into the `instructions` argument.
A direct or native call made inside `profile_override` may pass none; send
`profile.call_instructions(instructions)`, which falls back to the profile's
instructions for `None` and keeps an explicit empty string.

### Tools

```python title="chat_adapter.py"
    @contextmanager
    def tool_scope(self, tools: Sequence[object] = ()) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
        token = self._tools.set(tuple(tool for tool in tools if isinstance(tool, ToolSpec)))
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._tools.reset(token)

    def register_tool(self, tool: ToolSpec) -> None:
        self._tools.set((*self._tools.get(), tool))

    async def _execute(self, tools: dict[str, ToolSpec], call: ToolCall) -> str:
        tool = tools.get(call.name)
        if tool is None:
            return json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": f"Unknown tool {call.name!r}"})
        try:
            result = tool.fn(**validate_tool_arguments(tool, call.arguments))
            if inspect.isawaitable(result):
                result = await result
        except (ToolApprovalDenied, HookDeniedError) as exc:
            return json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": exc.message})
        except Exception as exc:
            message = correctable_tool_error(tool, exc)
            if message is None:
                raise
            return json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": message})
        return json.dumps({"ok": True, "result": to_jsonable_python(result, fallback=str)})

    @staticmethod
    def _declaration(tool: ToolSpec) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": tool.name,
            "description": tool.description or "",
            "parameters": tool.json_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
        }
```

`tool.fn` is already wrapped by Kedi. Calling it applies approval policy,
required-tool tracking, artifact admission, and telemetry. Some Kedi tools are
coroutines (subagent delegation is one), so always await an awaitable result.

Failures take one of three paths, the same ones Kedi's built-in adapters use:

- a denial (`ToolApprovalDenied`, or `HookDeniedError` from a `pre_tool_use`
  hook) goes back to the model as a failed result; the run continues;
- an error that `correctable_tool_error` classifies as correctable goes back
  to the model with Kedi's message;
- anything else, including budget exhaustion and cancellation, propagates and
  ends the run.

See [Errors, Retries, and Cancellation](errors.md).

### Calls

```python title="chat_adapter.py"
    async def _run(
        self,
        *,
        prompt: str,
        instructions: str | None,
        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None,
        history: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] = (),
        max_requests: int | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Reply, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
        messages = [*history, {"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in self._tools.get()}
        steps = self._max_steps if max_requests is None else min(self._max_steps, max_requests)
        for _ in range(steps):
            reply = await self._complete(
                BackendRequest(
                    model=self.active_profile.model or self._model,
                    instructions=instructions,
                    messages=list(messages),
                    tools=[self._declaration(tool) for tool in tools.values()],
                    output_schema=output_schema,
                    temperature=self.active_profile.settings.get("temperature"),
                )
            )
            report_invocation(
                InvocationUsage(
                    requests=1,
                    tool_calls=len(reply.tool_calls),
                    input_tokens=reply.input_tokens,
                    output_tokens=reply.output_tokens,
                    total_tokens=reply.input_tokens + reply.output_tokens,
                )
            )
            if not reply.tool_calls:
                content = reply.text if output_schema is None else json.dumps(reply.data)
                messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
                return reply, messages
            messages.append(
                {
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "tool_calls": [
                        {"id": call.id, "name": call.name, "arguments": call.arguments}
                        for call in reply.tool_calls
                    ],
                }
            )
            for call in reply.tool_calls:
                content = await self._execute(tools, call)
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": content})
        raise RuntimeError(f"{self.shortname} stopped after {steps} model requests")

    async def _complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        retries = request_retry_limit(self.active_profile.settings, self._request_retries)
        attempt = 0
        while True:
            admit_run_operation("request")
            try:
                return await self._backend.complete(request)
            except Exception as error:
                attempt += 1
                retry = await wait_for_request_retry(error, attempt=attempt, retries=retries)
                if not retry:
                    raise

    async def invoke(self, *, prompt: str, instructions: str | None = None, **_: Any) -> str:
        reply, _messages = await self._run(
            prompt=prompt, instructions=instructions, output_schema=None
        )
        if reply.text is None:
            raise RuntimeError("The backend returned no text")
        return reply.text

    async def produce(
        self,
        *,
        template: str,
        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        output_type: Any = None,
        instructions: str | None = None,
        **_: Any,
    ) -> Any:
        if output_schema is not None:
            schema = build_output_model(output_schema).model_json_schema()
        else:
            schema = TypeAdapter(output_type).json_schema()
        reply, _messages = await self._run(
            prompt=template, instructions=instructions, output_schema=schema
        )
        return reply.data

    def invoke_sync(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
        return run_sync(self.invoke(**kwargs))

    def produce_sync(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        return run_sync(self.produce(**kwargs))
```

The rules that matter:

- **One loop.** The synchronous entry points use `run_sync` from
  `kedi.agent_adapter.execution`, never `asyncio.run`. Kedi runs all
  overlapping model work on one shared event loop, and background subagents
  started by a tool call keep running on it after the call returns. A private
  loop would close under them. See [Concurrency and Event Loops](concurrency.md).
- **Kedi's text, unchanged.** `instructions` is the system message, the prompt
  is the user message, and the JSON Schema comes from `build_output_model`, so
  the field descriptions Kedi adds reach the model.
- **Usage after every request.** `report_invocation` feeds subagent usage
  limits, request-size reservations, telemetry, and checkpoint usage events.
  A subagent limit that is exceeded raises from inside `report_invocation`;
  let that exception propagate. Run budgets (`> budget:`) need one more call
  before each request: `admit_run_operation("request")`, which `_complete`
  calls before every attempt; see [Budgets and Usage](budgets.md).
- **Kedi validates.** `produce` returns the decoded value. Kedi checks it
  against the requested type, converts it, and fails the call if a field is
  missing.

## Running It

```python title="run_chat.py"
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Callable

from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class ScriptedBackend:
    """A test backend: each request is answered by a function of that request."""

    def __init__(self, answer: Callable[[BackendRequest], Reply]) -> None:
        self.answer = answer
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return self.answer(request)


def run(source: str, backend: ScriptedBackend) -> object:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=ChatAdapter(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        return runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
```

`runtime.aclose()` releases the runtime's resources after the run; it is not
model work, so `asyncio.run` is correct there.

A template capture with a tool:

```python title="run_chat.py"
from backend import ToolCall

SOURCE = """
@population(city: str) -> int:
  ###
  Return the population of a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `2_100_000`

> use: population
>> Paris has [count: int] inhabitants.
= `count`
"""


def answer(request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
    tool_results = [m for m in request.messages if m["role"] == "tool"]
    if not tool_results:
        return Reply(tool_calls=(ToolCall("c1", "population", {"city": "Paris"}),))
    return Reply(data={"count": 2_100_000})


backend = ScriptedBackend(answer)
assert run(SOURCE, backend) == 2_100_000
first = backend.requests[0]
assert first.model == "m1"
assert "<TemplateInstructions>" in (first.instructions or "")
assert first.output_schema is not None and "count" in first.output_schema["properties"]
assert "population" in {tool["name"] for tool in first.tools}
```

# Call Lifecycle

Every model call a program makes goes through the same sequence. This page
lists it step by step, with the adapter methods Kedi calls at each point, and
ends with a test that records the order on the [reference
adapter](reference-adapter.md).

## Which Statement Calls What

| Kedi statement | Entry point | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `[x] << ...` (untyped raw invoke) | `invoke_sync` | `prompt`, `instructions` |
| `[x: T] << ...` (typed raw invoke) | `produce_sync` | `template`, `output_type=T`, `instructions` |
| `>> ... [x] ... [y: T] ...` (template capture) | `produce_sync` | `template`, `output_schema`, `instructions` |
| `> if: <claim>` and `> loop: <claim>` conditions | `produce_sync` | `template`, `output_type` (an annotated `bool`), `instructions` |
| a child run started by `delegate_task` | `invoke` or `produce_subagent` (async) | see [Subagents](subagents.md) |

Kedi calls only keyword arguments. Accept unknown ones with `**kwargs`: new
keywords are added over time, and an adapter must not fail on one it ignores.

- `prompt` and `template` are the prompt Kedi rendered, not the source
  template. A template capture's prompt starts with Kedi's field list; a
  claim's prompt is `Claim: <text>`.
- `instructions` is the complete instruction text for the call, or `None` when
  there is none. See [Prompts and Instructions](prompt-contract.md).
- `produce_sync` receives exactly one of `output_schema` (a mapping from each
  output name to its resolved Kedi type) and `output_type` (a Python type).
  See [Structured Output](structured-output.md).

## The Sequence

For one call, Kedi:

1. **Resolves the call.** It freezes the active profile, resolves the
   adapter from `> adapter:` / `> agent:` or the compiled default, and
   resolves the call's tools: the profile's Kedi tools, deferred capability
   tools, skill tools, artifact tools, and delegation tools, each wrapped for
   approval, required-tool tracking, artifact admission, and telemetry.
2. **Checks the adapter against the profile.** `> requires:` capabilities,
   `> fallback:`, history processors, `tool_reason`, native compaction,
   CodeMode, and hook events are checked against `capabilities`. If the
   adapter does not implement `SupportsProfileOverride`, a profile that sets a
   model, effort, MCP servers, settings, compaction, or CodeMode fails with
   `AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported`. These checks raise before any model work.
3. **Opens a tool scope.** For an adapter with `SupportsToolRegistration`, it
   enters `tool_scope()` and calls `register_tool(spec)` for each tool, even
   when the call has none. The empty scope keeps a nested call from
   inheriting its caller's tools.
4. **Enters the profile.** For an adapter with `SupportsProfileOverride`, it
   enters `profile_override(profile)`.
5. **Checks multimodal input.** A prompt with images, audio, video, or
   documents and an adapter without
   `supports_media_input` fails with `MediaError: Adapter '<shortname>' does
   not accept media input`.
6. **Runs the prompt hook.** For an adapter based on `HookRegistrationMixin`,
   `user_prompt_submit` hooks run now and may replace the prompt text. See
   [Hooks](hooks.md).
7. **Assembles the request.** The prompt, instruction parts, tool
   definitions, output contract, and conversation coordinates become one
   immutable `AgentRunRequest`.
8. **Opens the conversation turn.** With history enabled, it reserves the
   next turn in the conversation; `> history: enabled` on an adapter without
   `supports_stateful_history` and `SupportsConversationState` fails with
   `Adapter '<shortname>' does not support stateful history`. See
   [Conversations and History](conversations.md).
9. **Checks the run budget and request size.** An active `> budget:` needs
   the matching budget capability. Kedi estimates the request's tokens from
   the prompt, instructions, tool schemas, output schema, media, and history,
   and reserves them against the profile's context limit. See [Budgets and
   Usage](budgets.md).
10. **Enters the request scopes**: required-tool tracking, artifact admission,
    the adapter's `conversation_scope(conversation)` when history is on, and
    the model-call telemetry span.
11. **Observes usage.** Every `report_invocation` from the adapter now feeds
    the request-size reservation, telemetry, and checkpoints.
12. **Calls the adapter**: `invoke_sync(prompt=..., instructions=...)` or
    `produce_sync(template=..., output_schema=... | output_type=...,
    instructions=...)`.
13. **Checks required tools.** If a tool marked `required_before_output` did
    not return successfully, the result is rejected with
    `RequiredToolCallError`.
14. **Validates the value.** For a template capture, every output name must be
    present (`LLM did not return required key: <name>`). Each explicitly typed
    field (`[x: T]`), each typed raw invoke, and each claim is validated and
    converted with `TypeAdapter(T).validate_python`. Untyped fields (`[x]`)
    are kept as returned.
15. **Commits.** With history, the turn is committed with the adapter's
    continuation state only now, after the value was accepted. On any
    exception the turn is cancelled and the continuation state is discarded.

Steps 13 to 15 belong to Kedi; an adapter never commits history or validates
the final value itself.

## Threads and Loops

A template capture or claim runs as a job on Kedi's execution engine, so
`produce_sync` is usually called on a worker thread, possibly for several
blocks at once. Raw invokes run on the calling thread. In both cases:

- keep per-call state in `ContextVar`s or in the scopes Kedi opens, never in
  plain attributes;
- run async work with `kedi.agent_adapter.execution.run_sync`, which uses
  Kedi's shared event loop; see [Concurrency and Event
  Loops](concurrency.md).

## Recording the Sequence

This adapter records each method Kedi calls on it:

```python title="run_lifecycle.py"
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Generator, Sequence
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any

from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class TracingAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    def __init__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.events: list[str] = []

    @contextmanager
    def tool_scope(self, tools: Sequence[object] = ()) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
        self.events.append("enter tool_scope")
        with super().tool_scope(tools):
            yield
        self.events.append("exit tool_scope")

    def register_tool(self, tool: Any) -> None:
        if tool.name == "population":
            self.events.append("register population")
        super().register_tool(tool)

    @contextmanager
    def profile_override(self, profile: Any) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
        self.events.append("enter profile_override")
        with super().profile_override(profile):
            yield
        self.events.append("exit profile_override")

    def produce_sync(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        self.events.append(f"produce_sync {sorted(kwargs)}")
        return super().produce_sync(**kwargs)


class Backend:
    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        if not any(m["role"] == "tool" for m in request.messages):
            return Reply(tool_calls=(ToolCall("c1", "population", {"city": "Paris"}),))
        return Reply(data={"count": 2_100_000})


SOURCE = """
@population(city: str) -> int:
  ###
  Return the population of a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `2_100_000`

> use: population
>> Paris has [count: int] inhabitants.
= `count`
"""

adapter = TracingAdapter(Backend(), model="m1")
runtime = compile_program(parse_program(SOURCE), adapter=adapter)
try:
    assert runtime.run_main() == 2_100_000
finally:
    asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())

assert adapter.events == [
    "enter tool_scope",
    "register population",
    "enter profile_override",
    "produce_sync ['instructions', 'output_schema', 'template']",
    "exit profile_override",
    "exit tool_scope",
], adapter.events
```

The scopes are strictly nested: tools are registered before the profile is
entered, both are open while the adapter runs, and both close in reverse
order after it returns.

---

Source: https://docs.kedi-lang.org/adapter-development/prompt-contract.md
Section: Adapter Development / Foundations

# Prompts and Instructions

Kedi writes every piece of text a model reads for a Kedi call. The adapter
sends that text to its backend unchanged. This page lists what the text
contains, in which order, and the few places where an adapter influences it.

## The Two Strings

Each call carries two strings:

| Argument | Send it as | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | the system or developer message | instruction parts, joined in order with a blank line |
| `prompt` (`invoke`) / `template` (`produce`) | the user message | the rendered prompt for this call |

Send each exactly once. Do not parse them, re-render them, translate them into
another format, or add text of your own around them.

## Instruction Parts

`instructions` is built from parts. Each has a stable identity and a source,
and appears only when it applies:

| Order | Identity | Source | Present when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `template.instructions` | runtime | the call is a template capture in completion mode; wrapped in `<TemplateInstructions>` |
| 2 | `profile.instructions` | profile | the profile has `> instructions:` |
| 3 | `capability:<identity>` | capability | an active capability contributes instructions |
| 4 | `grounding.instructions` | runtime | the profile has tools, MCP servers, or skills; wrapped in `<ToolCallInstructions>` |
| 5 | `skills.instructions` | skills | skills are enabled |
| 6 | `artifacts.instructions` | artifacts | the artifact contract is active for the call |
| 7 | `runtime.claim` | runtime | the call is a claim |
| 8 | `media_output.instructions` | runtime | the output or a tool's parameters take media, and the call attaches media or offers tools; wrapped in `<MediaOutputInstructions>` |

Two consequences for adapters:

- **The text is cache-stable.** Parts are ordered from the most stable to the
  most call-specific, and their content does not change between calls with the
  same profile and tools. Keep `instructions` first in the provider request so
  prompt caching works.
- **Profile instructions are already included.** Do not also read the
  profile's `> instructions:` from the active profile and send them; they would
  appear twice.

## The Prompt

| Call | Prompt |
|---|---|
| raw invoke `<<` | the rendered text of the statement |
| template capture, completion mode | `Fields to be substituted into the template string for final construction: (a, b).` followed by `The template string:` and the rendered template |
| template capture, decision mode | `Evaluate each marked decision field using its question, criteria, and the context below.` followed by the field list and the rendered template as context |
| claim | `Claim: <rendered claim>` |
| child run | the delegated task; see [Subagents](subagents.md) |

The completion rules (what a field value is, how to treat the surrounding
template text, escaped brackets, and so on) live in
`<TemplateInstructions>`, not in the prompt. Models that should not receive
them, such as a classifier, use decision mode.

## Decision Mode

An adapter chooses the template prompt mode per profile by implementing
`SupportsTemplatePromptMode`:

```python
from kedi.agent_adapter.meta import TemplatePromptMode
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile

def template_prompt_mode(self, profile: AgentProfile) -> TemplatePromptMode:
    return "completion"  # or "decision"
```

In decision mode the prompt asks the model to evaluate each field from the
context, and `template.instructions` is left out. Kedi's decision models
(TypeSafe Jev and Laya) use it. Adapters for general chat models do not
implement the protocol and get completion mode.

## Hook Edits

`user_prompt_submit` hooks run before the request is assembled. When a hook
replaces the prompt, the adapter receives the replaced text, and so do
telemetry, budgeting, cache identity, and history. The adapter must not apply
hooks again or keep a copy of the original prompt. See [Hooks](hooks.md).

## What an Adapter Must Not Add

- template-filling or field-extraction rules, examples, or reminders;
- output-format instructions such as "answer in JSON with fields ...": send
  the JSON Schema through the backend's structured-output feature instead (see
  [Structured Output](structured-output.md)). A backend without one declares
  `supports_native_structured_output=False`, and Kedi renders the output
  contract as the `protocol.output` part (see [Rendered Request](rendered-request.md));
- tool-usage instructions or tool catalogs: declare
  `supports_native_tool_calling=False` instead, and Kedi renders them as the
  `protocol.tools` part;
- a second copy of the profile instructions or of any part above;
- correction turns of its own. Send Kedi's: `output_correction`,
  `required_tools_correction` and `protocol_correction`, or the text
  `accept_subagent_output` gives for child results.

Text that identifies a harness and does not depend on the request, such as an
agent harness's own fixed system prompt, is not part of this contract.

## Seeing the Text

```python title="run_prompt_contract.py"
import asyncio
from typing import Any

from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self, reply: Reply) -> None:
        self.reply = reply
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return self.reply


def run(source: str, reply: Reply, adapter_type: type[ChatAdapter] = ChatAdapter) -> BackendRequest:
    backend = Recorder(reply)
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=adapter_type(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
    [request] = backend.requests
    return request


PROFILE = """
@lookup(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Look up facts about a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: read_only
  = `'facts'`

> instructions: Answer as a careful geographer.
> use: lookup
"""

capture = run(PROFILE + ">> The capital of France is [city].\n", Reply(data={"city": "Paris"}))
system = capture.instructions or ""
order = [
    system.index("<TemplateInstructions>"),
    system.index("Answer as a careful geographer."),
    system.index("<ToolCallInstructions>"),
]
assert order == sorted(order), system
assert capture.messages[0]["content"].startswith(
    "Fields to be substituted into the template string for final construction: (city)."
)
assert system.count("Answer as a careful geographer.") == 1

claim = run(PROFILE + "> if: Paris is in France\n  = yes\n", Reply(data=True))
claim_system = claim.instructions or ""
assert "<TemplateInstructions>" not in claim_system
assert claim_system.index("Answer as a careful") < claim_system.index("Determine whether")
assert claim.messages[0]["content"] == "Claim: Paris is in France"
```

A decision-mode adapter receives a different prompt and no completion rules:

```python title="run_prompt_contract.py"
class DecisionAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    def template_prompt_mode(self, profile: Any) -> str:
        return "decision"


decision = run(
    ">> The ticket [urgent: bool] needs a reply today.\n",
    Reply(data={"urgent": True}),
    DecisionAdapter,
)
assert decision.messages[0]["content"].startswith("Evaluate each marked decision field")
assert "<TemplateInstructions>" not in (decision.instructions or "")
```

# Rendered Request

Kedi renders every piece of text a model reads; the adapter transports it.
`current_request().render()` returns that text for the call in progress as one
value. It is the supported way for a custom adapter to build its backend
request.

## Reading the Request

```python
from kedi.agent_adapter import current_request

rendered = current_request().render()
```

`current_request()` is valid inside `invoke`, `produce` and their `_sync`
forms when Kedi makes the call. It raises `RuntimeError` outside a Kedi call,
and when Kedi calls `invoke`, `produce` or `produce_subagent` to run a subagent
child: the child runs inside its parent's request. `has_current_request()` says
which case applies, so an adapter that also runs children falls back to the
call's arguments:

```python
from kedi.agent_adapter import current_request, has_current_request

if has_current_request():
    rendered = current_request().render()
else:
    ...  # build the request from prompt or template, instructions and output_schema
```

| Field | Contents |
|---|---|
| `system` | the instruction parts joined with a blank line, verbatim; `None` when there are none |
| `instruction_parts` | the same parts, each with `identity`, `source` and `content` |
| `user` | the rendered prompt: the `prompt` or `template` argument |
| `media` | the prompt's attachments (see [Multimodal Input](multimodal-input.md)) |
| `output_json_schema` | the output schema Kedi built, with the model description and field descriptions; `None` for text |
| `output_tool_name` | `final_result` when there is an output schema, for a backend that takes the output as a tool call |
| `tools` | each tool's name, Kedi description, input and return schema, and `required_before_output`; `parameters` and `returns` give the schemas as plain JSON objects |
| `prompt_kind` | `raw`, `template` or `claim` |
| `call_kind` | `invoke` or `produce` |

Send `system` as the system or developer text, `user` with its `media` as the
user turn, the output schema as the backend's structured-output contract and
`tools` as its tool definitions. Without protocol parts, `system` is the same
text as the `instructions` argument.

## Backends Without Native Structured Output or Tool Calling

Some backends cannot take an output schema or tool definitions natively; a
small local model that only answers in text, for example. Declare it in the
capabilities:

```python
AdapterCapabilities(
    supports_structured_output=True,
    supports_tool_registration=True,
    supports_native_structured_output=False,
    supports_native_tool_calling=False,
)
```

`supports_structured_output` stays `True`: Kedi still asks the adapter for
structured values. The two new flags tell Kedi to render the contracts as text.
`render()` then appends Kedi-owned instruction parts after the others:

| Identity | Present when | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol.output` | `supports_native_structured_output=False` and the call has an output schema | `<OutputProtocol>`: answer with a JSON value matching the schema, and the schema itself |
| `protocol.tools` | `supports_native_tool_calling=False` and the call has tools | `<ToolProtocol>`: the call format, the final format, and `<Tools>`, each tool's description and schemas |

The model answers with one JSON object per turn:

- `{"action": "call_tool", "callId": "c1", "name": "lookup", "arguments": {...}}` to call a tool;
- `{"action": "final", "data": ...}` with the output value, or `{"action": "final", "text": "..."}` for a text call.

The adapter parses that object and runs tools as usual. It never writes this
text itself; the wording is versioned (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` in
`kedi.agent_adapter.request.prompts`). The protocol parts are not part of the
`instructions` argument, so hooks and telemetry see the instructions they
always saw.

An adapter that adds tools during the run, from MCP servers for example, passes
its final tool set so the catalog names them too:

```python
from kedi.agent_adapter.request import tool_definition

rendered = current_request().render(tools=tuple(tool_definition(spec) for spec in specs))
```

## Corrections

Corrections are Kedi's text too. `kedi.agent_adapter.request.prompts` has one
function for each:

| Function | Send it as a user turn when |
|---|---|
| `output_correction(error)` | the answer fails the output schema; `error` is the validation error |
| `required_tools_correction(missing, attempted=...)` | the model answers before a tool with `required_before_output` completed; `attempted` is whether it tried |
| `protocol_correction(detail)` | the answer is not one protocol action; `detail` is your parse error |

Take required tools from `ToolDefinition.required_before_output`. Do not infer
them from the prompt.

## Scenario

The adapter below forwards the rendered request to a text-only backend and
parses its JSON action.

```python title="rendered_adapter.py"
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from typing import Any

from pydantic import TypeAdapter

from kedi.agent_adapter import AdapterCapabilities, AgentAdapterKind, current_request
from kedi.agent_adapter.request.prompts import output_correction


class PromptedAdapter:
    """A backend that reads text and answers with one JSON action."""

    kind: AgentAdapterKind = "agent-framework"
    shortname = "prompted"
    capabilities = AdapterCapabilities(
        supports_structured_output=True,
        supports_native_structured_output=False,
        supports_native_tool_calling=False,
    )

    def __init__(self, answers: list[str]) -> None:
        self.answers = answers
        self.sent: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def invoke_sync(self, *, prompt: str, **_: Any) -> str:
        return str(self._answer(None))

    def produce_sync(self, *, template: str, output_type: Any = None, **_: Any) -> Any:
        return self._answer(TypeAdapter(output_type))

    def _answer(self, validator: TypeAdapter[Any] | None) -> Any:
        rendered = current_request().render()
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": rendered.user}]
        for answer in self.answers:
            self.sent.append({"system": rendered.system, "messages": list(messages)})
            action = json.loads(answer)
            if validator is None:
                return action["text"]
            try:
                return validator.validate_python(action["data"])
            except ValueError as error:
                messages += [
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": answer},
                    {"role": "user", "content": output_correction(error)},
                ]
        raise RuntimeError("no valid answer")
```

```python title="run_rendered_request.py"
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from rendered_adapter import PromptedAdapter

adapter = PromptedAdapter(['{"action": "final", "data": "three"}', '{"action": "final", "data": 3}'])
runtime = compile_program(
    parse_program("[count: int] << How many sides has a triangle?\n= `count`\n"), adapter=adapter
)
assert runtime.run_main() == 3

first, second = adapter.sent
assert first["system"].startswith("<OutputProtocol>\n")
assert '<OutputSchema>{"type": "integer"}</OutputSchema>' in first["system"]
assert first["messages"] == [{"role": "user", "content": "How many sides has a triangle?"}]
correction = second["messages"][-1]["content"]
assert correction.startswith("The structured output does not match the required schema:")
```

The first answer fails the schema, so the adapter sends Kedi's correction and the
second answer is accepted.

Source: https://docs.kedi-lang.org/adapter-development/structured-output.md
Section: Adapter Development / Foundations

# Structured Output

`produce` and `produce_sync` return values, not text. Kedi says what the value
must look like in one of two ways, the adapter asks the backend for it, and
Kedi validates what comes back.

## The Two Contracts

| Argument | Sent for | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `output_schema` | template captures (`>> ... [a] ... [b: T] ...`) | `dict[str, ResolvedKediType]`: one entry per output name, in template order |
| `output_type` | typed raw invokes (`[x: T] << ...`) and claims | a Python type: `T`, or `Annotated[bool, Field(description=...)]` for a claim |

Exactly one of them is set. `ResolvedKediType` is Kedi's resolved form of a
field type, including `Annotated` descriptions, constraints, `Literal`
choices, custom `~Type`s, and generics. Do not interpret it yourself; turn it
into a JSON Schema with Kedi's helpers.

## Building the JSON Schema

```python
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from kedi.agent_adapter.output_schema import build_output_model

if output_schema is not None:
    schema = build_output_model(output_schema).model_json_schema()
else:
    schema = TypeAdapter(output_type).json_schema()
```

`build_output_model` builds the Pydantic model Kedi's own adapters send:

- one field per output name, with the field's type, description, and
  constraints;
- names that Pydantic cannot use as attributes (a leading underscore,
  `model_...`, or a `BaseModel` member) become internal field names with the
  Kedi name as the alias, so the JSON property is still the Kedi name;
- fixed-length tuples are expressed with `items` instead of `prefixItems`,
  which most model APIs reject;
- for template captures in completion mode, a model description that tells
  the model to return only the replacement values.

Call it inside `produce`: the description depends on the active request.

## Non-Object Roots

A claim's schema is a bare boolean, and a typed raw invoke's schema is
whatever `T` is: `{"type": "integer"}`, an array, an enum. Many structured
output APIs accept only an object at the root. For such a backend, wrap the
schema in one property and unwrap the answer:

```python title="object_root.py"
from typing import Any

from pydantic import TypeAdapter

from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter
from kedi.agent_adapter.output_schema import build_output_model


class ObjectRootAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    async def produce(
        self,
        *,
        template: str,
        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        output_type: Any = None,
        instructions: str | None = None,
        **_: Any,
    ) -> Any:
        if output_schema is not None:
            schema = build_output_model(output_schema).model_json_schema()
            reply, _messages = await self._run(
                prompt=template, instructions=instructions, output_schema=schema
            )
            return reply.data
        value_schema = TypeAdapter(output_type).json_schema()
        wrapped = {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"result": value_schema},
            "required": ["result"],
            "additionalProperties": False,
        }
        reply, _messages = await self._run(
            prompt=template, instructions=instructions, output_schema=wrapped
        )
        return reply.data["result"]
```

Move `$defs` to the wrapper's root if your backend does not resolve
references below the root.

## Return Values

| Call | Return |
|---|---|
| `output_schema` | a mapping, or an object with one attribute per output name |
| `output_type` | the value |

Return the decoded JSON. Then Kedi:

1. reads every output name from the result; a missing one fails the call with
   `LLM did not return required key: <name>`;
2. validates and converts each **explicitly typed** field (`[x: T]`), each
   typed raw invoke, and each claim with `TypeAdapter(T).validate_python`, so
   a JSON object becomes the program's `~Type` instance and `"3"` becomes `3`
   for an `int`;
3. keeps **untyped** fields (`[x]`) exactly as returned. Their schema type is
   `string`; return a string.

Do not convert values into Kedi types inside the adapter, and do not return
provider message or response objects.

## JSON Schema Formats

`supported_json_schema_formats` declares which JSON Schema `format` values the
backend enforces, for example `frozenset({"date", "date-time"})`. The Kedi
language server uses it for built-in adapters to flag field types that would
produce an unsupported format (`K-ADAPTER-SCHEMA-FORMAT`). Leave it `None`
when the backend accepts any format; Kedi still validates the returned value
against the full type.

## Advertising Structured Output

Set `supports_structured_output=True` only when the backend constrains the
answer to the schema, including nested objects, lists, unions, and
constraints. An adapter that only asks for JSON in the prompt does not support
structured output and must not write such a prompt either (see [Prompts and
Instructions](prompt-contract.md)). A program can demand the capability with
`> requires: structured_output`, which fails before any model call when the
adapter does not advertise it.

## Running It

```python title="run_structured_output.py"
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Callable

from kedi.errors import KediExecutionError
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter
from object_root import ObjectRootAdapter


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self, answer: Callable[[BackendRequest], Reply]) -> None:
        self.answer = answer
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return self.answer(request)


def run(source: str, answer: Callable[[BackendRequest], Reply], adapter_type=ChatAdapter):
    backend = Recorder(answer)
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=adapter_type(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        return runtime.run_main(), backend.requests
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())


CAPTURE = """
~Airport(code: str, runways: int)

>> [city] has [airports: list[Airport]] and [population: int] inhabitants.
= `(city, airports, population)`
"""

value, [request] = run(
    CAPTURE,
    lambda _r: Reply(
        data={
            "city": "Paris",
            "airports": [{"code": "CDG", "runways": 4}],
            "population": "2100000",
        }
    ),
)
city, airports, population = value
assert city == "Paris"
assert airports[0].code == "CDG" and airports[0].runways == 4
assert population == 2_100_000
schema = request.output_schema
assert list(schema["properties"]) == ["city", "airports", "population"]
assert schema["properties"]["population"]["type"] == "integer"
assert "replacement values" in schema["description"]
```

A missing field fails the call:

```python title="run_structured_output.py"
try:
    run(CAPTURE, lambda _r: Reply(data={"city": "Paris", "airports": []}))
except KediExecutionError as error:
    assert "LLM did not return required key: population" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("a missing field must fail")
```

A claim through a backend that needs an object root:

```python title="run_structured_output.py"
CLAIM = """
[answer] = `'no'`
> if: Paris is in France
  [answer] := yes
= <answer>
"""

value, [request] = run(CLAIM, lambda _r: Reply(data={"result": True}), ObjectRootAdapter)
assert value == "yes"
assert request.output_schema["properties"]["result"]["type"] == "boolean"
assert "claim is established" in request.output_schema["properties"]["result"]["description"]
```

# Errors, Retries, and Cancellation

An adapter meets three kinds of failure: a tool call fails, a backend request
fails, or the run is cancelled. Kedi decides which failures the model may see
and correct, which ones are retried, and which ones end the program. The
adapter follows those decisions with three helpers.

## Tool Failures

When `tool.fn(**arguments)` raises, the adapter must pick one of three paths:

| Failure | Path | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `ToolApprovalDenied` (approval policy) or `HookDeniedError` (`pre_tool_use` hook) | return `exc.message` to the model as a failed tool result | `Tool 'delete_file' was denied: static deny policy` |
| `correctable_tool_error(tool, exc)` returns a message | return that message to the model | `Tool lookup failed: ValueError: unknown city. Correct the arguments if they caused this, or continue without this result.` |
| `correctable_tool_error(tool, exc)` returns `None` | re-raise; the program call fails | a `RuntimeError` in a procedure, `RunBudgetExceeded`, run cancellation |

`kedi.agent_adapter.tools.errors.correctable_tool_error(tool, exc)` is the
classification Kedi's built-in adapters use. It returns Kedi's model-facing
message for:

- application tools (Kedi procedures and Python tools) that raise
  `ValueError`, `LookupError`, or `OSError`: rejected input, a missing record,
  unreachable data;
- Kedi's own tool families: subagent delegation and lifecycle, dynamic
  workflows, artifact management, filesystem and terminal tools, CodeMode
  controls, and capability activation;

and `None` for budget exhaustion (`RunBudgetExceeded`), cancellation, failures
after a tool already returned, and every other exception. Do not write your
own classification or your own message; a message from this function is the
text the model should read.

Kedi's errors (`KediExecutionError` and its subclasses, including both denial
types) render a Kedi stack trace in `str(exc)`. Send `exc.message`, the plain
message, to the model.

The reference adapter's `_execute` implements exactly this table. A framework
with a tool-retry envelope (Pydantic AI's `ModelRetry`, LangChain's
`ToolMessage` with an error status) carries the same message through that
envelope instead of a JSON result.

## Request Failures

A backend request can fail transiently: a rate limit, an overloaded server, a
timeout. Retry only the request, never the whole run, and never a tool call:

```python
from kedi.agent_adapter.request_retry import wait_for_request_retry

attempt = 0
while True:
    try:
        return await backend.complete(request)
    except Exception as error:
        attempt += 1
        if not await wait_for_request_retry(error, attempt=attempt, retries=retries):
            raise
```

`wait_for_request_retry(error, attempt=, retries=)`:

- returns `False` when `attempt > retries` or the error is not transient;
- treats an error as transient when it has an integer `status_code` of 408,
  429, or 5xx, so keep the provider's exception (or give yours a
  `status_code`);
- waits for the provider's `Retry-After` (read from `error.response.headers`,
  following `__cause__`), or for exponential backoff from 0.5 s, and returns
  `True`;
- returns `False` instead of waiting longer than 30 seconds.

Kedi's built-in adapters default to two retries and read the
`request_retries` setting; `request_retry_limit(settings, default)` validates
that setting. Report usage only for requests that completed.

When the request finally fails, raise. Kedi wraps the exception in a
`KediExecutionError` with the Kedi source location and keeps the original as
`error.original`, so the retry policy of the job-manager engine can still
classify a `429` or a timeout. Never turn a failed request into an empty
result, and never fall back to a text request after a structured one failed.

## Cancellation

A run is cancelled when the program's caller cancels it, when a parent cancels
a child, when a CodeMode or workflow sandbox stops, or when an interrupt
supersedes a child attempt. Cancellation arrives as `asyncio.CancelledError`
in the adapter's coroutine, or as `RunCancelled` when synchronous work checks
`check_run_cancelled()`.

- Let both propagate. Do not catch `BaseException` or `asyncio.CancelledError`
  to return a value.
- Release what the call owns in `finally`: streams, sessions, subprocesses.
  `run_sync` gives the cancelled coroutine time to clean up.
- A cancelled call must not write continuation state (`result_state`) or
  report a result; Kedi discards the turn.
- A cancellation request is not proof that a remote side effect was undone.
  Do not report one as reversed.

## Error Messages

Raise errors that name the adapter and the failing part:

| Situation | Raise |
|---|---|
| a profile field the adapter does not support | `AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported` from `profile_override` |
| an MCP transport the backend cannot open | `ValueError` naming the transport, before the request |
| the backend returned no text or no structured value | `RuntimeError` naming the adapter |
| a protocol or stream error from the backend | the provider's exception, or one chained to it with `from` |

## Running It

```python title="run_errors.py"
import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import Callable

from kedi.errors import KediExecutionError
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply, ToolCall
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Scripted:
    def __init__(self, answer: Callable[[BackendRequest], Reply]) -> None:
        self.answer = answer
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return self.answer(request)


def run(source: str, backend) -> object:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=ChatAdapter(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        return runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())


def tool_program(body: str, approval: str = "allow", risk: str = "read_only") -> str:
    return f"""
@lookup(city: str) -> str:
  ###
  Look up a city.
  ###
  > tool:
    risk: {risk}
  = `{body}`

> approval: {approval}
> use: lookup
[answer] << Look up Atlantis.
= <answer>
"""


def call_then_echo(request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
    results = [json.loads(m["content"]) for m in request.messages if m["role"] == "tool"]
    if not results:
        return Reply(tool_calls=(ToolCall("c1", "lookup", {"city": "Atlantis"}),))
    return Reply(text=results[0]["error"])
```

A correctable failure reaches the model with Kedi's message:

```python title="run_errors.py"
answer = run(tool_program("(_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError('unknown city'))"), Scripted(call_then_echo))
assert answer.startswith("Tool lookup failed: ValueError: unknown city."), answer
```

A denial reaches the model, and the run continues:

```python title="run_errors.py"
answer = run(tool_program("'ok'", approval="deny", risk="mutating"), Scripted(call_then_echo))
assert "was denied" in answer, answer
```

Any other failure ends the call:

```python title="run_errors.py"
try:
    run(tool_program("(_ for _ in ()).throw(RuntimeError('database is down'))"), Scripted(call_then_echo))
except KediExecutionError as error:
    assert "database is down" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an unclassified tool failure must end the call")
```

A rate limit is retried; a bad request is not:

```python title="run_errors.py"
class ProviderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status_code: int) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status_code}")
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.response = type("Response", (), {"headers": {"retry-after": "0"}})()


class Flaky:
    def __init__(self, status_code: int) -> None:
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.calls = 0

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.calls += 1
        if self.calls == 1:
            raise ProviderError(self.status_code)
        return Reply(text="ok")


flaky = Flaky(429)
assert run("[answer] << Say ok.\n= <answer>\n", flaky) == "ok"
assert flaky.calls == 2

rejected = Flaky(400)
try:
    run("[answer] << Say ok.\n= <answer>\n", rejected)
except KediExecutionError as error:
    assert isinstance(error.original, ProviderError)
else:
    raise AssertionError("a 400 must not be retried")
assert rejected.calls == 1
```

# Profiles, Models, and Settings

A program configures each call through its active profile: `> model:`,
`> effort:`, `> settings:`, `> fallback:`, `> mcp:`, and the profile
directives that select tools, approval, history, and children. The adapter
sees the profile only if it implements `SupportsProfileOverride`.

## The Protocol

`kedi.agent_adapter.meta.SupportsProfileOverride`:

```python
from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfile

def default_model(self) -> str | None: ...

def profile_override(self, profile: AgentProfile) -> AbstractContextManager[None]: ...
```

- `default_model()` returns the model the adapter uses when the profile sets
  none. Kedi records it in telemetry and run records.
- `profile_override(profile)` applies `profile` to every call made inside the
  context and restores the previous profile on exit. Kedi enters it around
  each call (see [Call Lifecycle](call-lifecycle.md)), and the adapter enters
  it for a child in `subagent_scope` (see [Subagents](subagents.md)).
  Overrides nest, so keep a stack in a `ContextVar`, as the [reference
  adapter](reference-adapter.md#profiles) does.

## Without the Protocol

An adapter that does not implement `SupportsProfileOverride` runs every call
with its own configuration. Kedi then refuses, before the call, any profile
that sets a model, fallback models, effort, MCP servers, settings, compaction,
or CodeMode:

```text
AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported: Active adapter does not support agent profile override
(requested model=..., effort=..., ...)
```

`> instructions:`, tools, approval, and children need no override: they reach
the adapter as `instructions`, registered tools, wrapped tools, and
delegation tools.

## With the Protocol

Once the adapter implements the protocol, Kedi stops refusing profile fields
for it. The adapter must refuse every field it cannot honor, in
`profile_override`, with `AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported` naming the field.
Silently ignoring a field runs the program with a configuration it did not
ask for.

| Profile field | Directive | Adapter's job |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `> model:` | Use it instead of `default_model()`. Advertise `supports_model_override`. |
| `effort` | `> effort:` | Map the level to the backend, or refuse it. Advertise `supports_effort`. |
| `settings` | `> settings:` | Apply the names listed in `capabilities.settings`; refuse other names except Kedi's own. Advertise `supports_settings`. |
| `fallback_models` | `> fallback:` | Try the alternatives on transient failures. Advertise `supports_model_fallback`; Kedi refuses `> fallback:` otherwise. |
| `mcp_servers` | `> mcp:` | Connect the servers, or refuse them. See [MCP, Skills, and Capability Tools](mcp-and-skills.md). |
| profile instructions | `> instructions:` | Nothing: Kedi renders them into the `instructions` argument. Do not read them from the profile. |
| `approval`, `hooks`, `history`, `artifacts`, `run_budget`, `compaction`, `codemode` | | Owned by Kedi; the capability pages say what the adapter must add. |

Kedi still checks capability-gated features for every adapter before the call:
`> requires:`, `> fallback:` (`model_fallback`), history processors, native
compaction, CodeMode, hook events, and `tool_reason`.

## Effort

`effort` is one of `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`
(`kedi.effort.EffortValue`). Map it onto the backend's reasoning control. When
the backend has fewer levels, map to the nearest one and document it; Kedi's
Pydantic AI adapter maps `max` to `xhigh` (`kedi.effort.pydantic_effort_value`).
When the backend has no reasoning control, refuse `effort` rather than
dropping it.

## Settings

Kedi knows the settings that it and the built-in adapters accept (see
[the settings inventory](../agentic-engineering/instructions-and-settings.md#settings-inventory)).
A custom adapter declares the names it applies, from those or of its own, such
as a `reasoning_budget` its backend takes:

```python
capabilities = AdapterCapabilities(
    supports_settings=True,
    settings=frozenset({"temperature", "reasoning_budget"}),
)
```

Kedi refuses a name the adapter does not declare before the first model request:
`adapter '<shortname>' does not take the settings <names>`.

Five settings belong to Kedi and may appear in any profile
(`kedi.agent_profile.settings.KEDI_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS`):

| Setting | Owner | Adapter's job |
|---|---|---|
| `context_limit` | Kedi's request-size check | none |
| `media_limit` | Kedi's media check | none |
| `request_retries` | the adapter's request retries | read it with `request_retry_limit(settings, default)` |
| `tool_reason` | approval reasons | only adapters that list `tool_reason` in `capabilities.settings` may receive it; Kedi refuses it for the others |
| `voice` | speech output | an adapter with `supports_audio_output` reads it with `speech_voice(settings)` |

## Model Fallback

`fallback_models` is an ordered tuple of model IDs. Kedi's adapters try the
next model when a request to the current one fails with a transient provider
error (`kedi.agent_adapter.request_retry.transient_provider_error`: status
408, 429, or 5xx), per request, after request retries are exhausted. They do
not fall back after a response has started streaming, and an alternative
never replaces an unresolved primary model.

## Running It

```python title="run_profiles.py"
import asyncio

from kedi.agent_adapter import MissingAdapterCapabilityError
from kedi.agent_profile import AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Recorder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.requests: list[BackendRequest] = []

    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        self.requests.append(request)
        return Reply(text="ok")


def run(source: str) -> list[BackendRequest]:
    backend = Recorder()
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=ChatAdapter(backend, model="m1"))
    try:
        runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())
    return backend.requests


[default] = run("[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
assert default.model == "m1"

[fast] = run(
    "> profile: fast:\n"
    "    > model: m-fast\n"
    "    > settings:\n"
    "        temperature: 0.2\n"
    "> use: fast\n"
    "[a] << Hi.\n"
    "= <a>\n"
)
assert fast.model == "m-fast" and fast.temperature == 0.2

for directive, field in (
    ("> effort: high", "effort"),
    ("> settings:\n    max_tokens: 10", "max_tokens"),
):
    try:
        run(f"{directive}\n[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
    except Exception as error:
        assert isinstance(error, AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported) or isinstance(
            getattr(error, "original", None), AgentProfileOverrideUnsupported
        ), error
        assert field in str(error)
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"{field} must be refused")

try:
    run("> model: m1\n> fallback: m2\n[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n")
except Exception as error:
    assert "model_fallback" in str(error), error
    assert isinstance(error, MissingAdapterCapabilityError) or isinstance(
        getattr(error, "original", None), MissingAdapterCapabilityError
    )
else:
    raise AssertionError("fallback needs supports_model_fallback")
```

Source: https://docs.kedi-lang.org/adapter-development/capabilities.md
Section: Adapter Development / Foundations

# Capability Reference

`AdapterCapabilities` (`kedi.agent_adapter.AdapterCapabilities`) is the
adapter's declaration of what it implements. Kedi reads it before relying on
an optional protocol, `> requires:` checks it before any model I/O, and the
language server and `kedi explain` read it for built-in adapters.

## Values

Most fields are `bool | None`:

| Value | Meaning | Kedi |
|---|---|---|
| `True` | implemented and tested | relies on it |
| `False` | not implemented | refuses programs that need it |
| `None` | unknown, for example until a remote peer is asked | refuses it, unless the name is in `negotiated_capabilities` |

Declare only what the adapter really implements, not what the underlying SDK
could do. A capability that Kedi relies on but the adapter only approximates
fails in ways Kedi cannot detect.

## Fields

| Field | Means the adapter | Kedi, when it is `True` | When a program needs it and it is not `True` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supports_structured_output` | constrains answers to a JSON Schema | — | `> requires: structured_output` fails |
| `supports_tool_registration` | implements `tool_scope` / `register_tool` | registers each call's tools | tools on an adapter without the protocol: `AgentToolOverrideUnsupported: Active adapter does not support tool registration` |
| `supports_capabilities` | applies `> capability:` bundles | — (Kedi merges a bundle's instructions and tools into the profile; using one adds an implicit `capabilities` requirement) | `MissingAdapterCapabilityError` for `capabilities` |
| `supports_deferred_tools` | activates `defer: true` capability tools on demand | registers tools with a pending `deferred_capability` | `MissingAdapterCapabilityError` for `deferred_tools` |
| `supports_mcp` | connects profile MCP servers | — (`mcp_servers` reaches the adapter through the profile either way) | `> requires: mcp` fails; the adapter must refuse servers it cannot open |
| `supports_profile_override` | implements `SupportsProfileOverride` | — (the protocol, not the flag, is checked at run time) | `> requires: profile_override` fails |
| `supports_model_override` | honors `> model:` | — | `> requires: model_override` fails |
| `supports_model_fallback` | tries `> fallback:` models on transient failures | passes `fallback_models` | `> fallback:` fails with `MissingAdapterCapabilityError` for `model_fallback` |
| `supports_effort` | honors `> effort:` | — | `> requires: effort` fails |
| `supports_settings` | honors the names in `settings` | — | `> requires: settings` fails |
| `settings` | the accepted setting names | allows `tool_reason`, and names Kedi does not know, only when listed | `tool_reason is not supported by adapter '<shortname>'`; `adapter '<shortname>' does not take the settings <names>` |
| `supports_codemode` | runs the CodeMode controls, or, on a JSON-RPC bridge, its backend's own code mode | allows `> codemode:` | `CodeMode is not supported by adapter '<shortname>'` |
| `supports_native_approvals` | applies approval policies itself | stops wrapping tools with approval; passes `approval_ceiling` to children | — |
| `supports_native_approval_handler` | drives an interactive approval handler natively | — | `> requires: native_approval_handler` fails |
| `supports_subagents` | runs children (`SupportsSubagentExecution`) | offers `delegate_task` and `continue_subagent` | `AgentSubagentUnsupported: Active adapter does not support Kedi subagent delegation` |
| `supports_background_subagents` | lets children run while the parent continues | offers `background`, `wait_subagent`, `cancel_subagent`, `subagent_status` | `background: true` fails as a tool error |
| `supports_live_subagent_input` | delivers input to running children | offers `send_subagent_input`, `send_parent_message` | `> requires: live_subagent_input` fails |
| `supports_subagent_interrupt` | stops and restarts a child attempt | accepts `interrupt: true` | `> requires: subagent_interrupt` fails |
| `supports_artifacts` | passes Kedi tool results through unchanged and registers artifact tools | adds the artifact contract to calls with tools | a call with tools fails: `ArtifactCapabilityError: Active adapter does not support Kedi artifact references and tools` |
| `supports_native_artifacts` | admits adapter-native and MCP tool results before they enter history | — | `> requires: native_artifacts` fails |
| `supports_stateful_history` | continues native conversations (`SupportsConversationState`) | enters `conversation_scope` and keeps continuation state | `> history: enabled` fails: `Adapter '<shortname>' does not support stateful history` |
| `supports_history_replay` | rebuilds the full causal message sequence from Kedi history | — | `> requires: history_replay` fails |
| `supports_history_processing` | runs history processors | allows processors and conditions | `MissingAdapterCapabilityError` for `history_processing` |
| `supports_native_compaction` | compacts history natively | allows `compaction: native` | `native compaction is not supported by adapter '<shortname>'` |
| `supports_stream_events` | emits streaming events | — | `> requires: stream_events` fails |
| `supports_request_budget` | admits each model request against the run budget | allows `> budget: request_limit` | `Adapter '<shortname>' cannot enforce request run budget for this execution` |
| `supports_token_usage` | reports the provider's token counts with each invocation (see [Reporting Usage](budgets.md#reporting-usage)) | — | a child with token limits fails before it runs: `Adapter '<shortname>' reports no token usage, so the subagent <limits> cannot be enforced` |
| `supports_tool_attempt_budget` | admits each tool attempt against the run budget | allows `> budget: tool_attempt_limit` (not with MCP or external tools) | `Adapter '<shortname>' cannot enforce tool_attempt run budget for this execution` |
| `supports_media_input` | accepts multimodal input: places prompt images, audio, video, and documents in the request | allows multimodal prompts | `MediaError: Adapter '<shortname>' does not accept media input` |
| `supports_image_output` | returns an `Image` for `[img: Image] << ...`: one the model draws, or one of the request's media it names | allows image output | the model can only name an attached image; a request with none fails: `MediaError: Adapter '<shortname>' cannot produce images` |
| `supports_audio_output` | returns an `Audio` for `[speech: Audio] << ...`, from a model that speaks; the request carries no media and no tools | allows speech output | `MediaError: Adapter '<shortname>' cannot produce speech` |
| `supports_native_structured_output` | `False`: the backend cannot take an output schema natively | adds the `protocol.output` part to `render()` (see [Rendered Request](rendered-request.md)) | — |
| `supports_native_tool_calling` | `False`: the backend cannot take tool definitions natively | adds the `protocol.tools` part to `render()`: the tool catalog and the call format | — |
| `hooks` | dispatches the listed hook events (`HookCapabilities`) | runs profile hooks | `Agent hooks are not supported by adapter '<shortname>'`, or `Agent hook events <names> are not supported` |
| `supported_json_schema_formats` | enforces these JSON Schema `format`s | the language server flags other formats for built-in adapters | — |
| `negotiated_capabilities` | checks these `None` capabilities itself, before remote work | lets `> requires:` pass for them | — |

A `—` in the third column means Kedi changes nothing at run time; the flag
still answers `> requires:`, the language server, and `kedi explain`.

## Invariants

The constructor enforces two dependencies:

- `supports_artifacts=True` requires `supports_structured_output=True` and
  `supports_tool_registration=True`;
- `supports_native_artifacts=True` requires `supports_artifacts=True`.

## `> requires:` and Negotiation

```kedi
> requires:
    structured_output
    tool_registration
```

Kedi checks each requirement against `capability_status(name)`:

- `True` passes;
- `False` fails with `MissingAdapterCapabilityError: Adapter '<shortname>'
  does not satisfy required capability '<name>'`;
- `None` fails too, unless the name is in `negotiated_capabilities`. An adapter
  that can only learn a capability from its peer, such as an A2A adapter
  reading an Agent Card, lists it there and must refuse the request itself,
  before starting remote work, when the peer turns out not to support it.

## Built-in Shortnames

The language server and `kedi explain` resolve capabilities from the adapter
registry, by shortname. An adapter passed as an instance
(`compile_program(adapter=...)`) is known only at run time, so its
capabilities produce run-time errors, not editor diagnostics.

## Running It

```python title="run_capabilities.py"
import asyncio
from dataclasses import replace

from kedi.agent_adapter import MissingAdapterCapabilityError
from kedi.lang import compile_program, parse_program

from backend import BackendRequest, Reply
from chat_adapter import ChatAdapter


class Echo:
    async def complete(self, request: BackendRequest) -> Reply:
        return Reply(text="ok")


def run(source: str, adapter: ChatAdapter) -> object:
    runtime = compile_program(parse_program(source), adapter=adapter)
    try:
        return runtime.run_main()
    finally:
        asyncio.run(runtime.aclose())


SOURCE = "> requires:\n    tool_registration\n    stream_events\n[a] << Hi.\n= <a>\n"

try:
    run(SOURCE, ChatAdapter(Echo(), model="m1"))
except MissingAdapterCapabilityError as error:
    assert error.requirement == "stream_events"
    assert "does not satisfy required capability 'stream_events'" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("stream_events is unknown, so it must fail")


class NegotiatingAdapter(ChatAdapter):
    capabilities = replace(
        ChatAdapter.capabilities, negotiated_capabilities=frozenset({"stream_events"})
    )


assert run(SOURCE, NegotiatingAdapter(Echo(), model="m1")) == "ok"
```
